records.reason: m146 at 2/1 and 50 uL fills a low-to-intermediate response point between the measured 0/1 anchor 65723de539453b98b181 and the measured 2/1, 100 uL point 2745c6978a8911fc3dda. It separates solvent-response curvature from loading movement before the sharp transition.

m146 at 5/1 and 50 uL is a loading contrast to the measured 5/1, 100 uL point 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e and samples the transition before the measured 10/1 points. It can teach whether loading primarily moves onset or also broadens the finish.

m206 at 1/1 and 50 uL supplies a missing pretransition point between the measured 0/1 point 035c26f2979b6bb5c0b5 and 2/1 point 7c0c324643799c918828. This constrains the onset of the scaffold-specific rise.

m206 at 5/1 and 50 uL complements measured 5/1 points 614873124b33029a924c and cdf40bcb3f4392f8d7d1 at larger loadings. The result tests whether the intermediate transition has a loading-dependent endpoint asymmetry.

m90 at 2/1 and 100 uL fills the pyridyl ester curve between the measured 2/1, 150 uL point 22f82413c75481d74e9b, the 5/1 point b51b5dbcd2a38b174973, and the high-ratio failure 96710afeabc594baa359. It is a direct graph-condition transfer test.

m90 at 10/1 and 150 uL is a loading contrast to the measured 10/1, 100 uL failure 96710afeabc594baa359. Its high current width makes the endpoint response at strong solvent especially consequential for retraining.

m205 at 0/1 and 150 uL provides a low-strength anchor for the naphthylethanol scaffold after the large measured errors at 2/1 and 5/1 in c973d4c257be9ef08216 and 48853fd78c77153b963a. It tests whether the delayed retention is intrinsic or emerges only at stronger solvent.

m205 at 1/1 and 50 uL probes the early rise and loading surface below the measured 2/1 point c973d4c257be9ef08216 and the broad 5/1 loading pair centered on 48853fd78c77153b963a. This can anchor transfer to related aromatic alcohols.

m119 at 0/1 and 50 uL adds a low-retention anchor to the broad measured 5/1 responses 776ee2c1e85ebde75168 and e6e78489d1da4066c07e. It tests whether the broad interval develops gradually or after a threshold.

m119 at 2/1 and 150 uL samples the developing region between its low-strength behavior and the measured 5/1 loading contrast. The label can distinguish finish-dominant broadening from a simple onset shift.

m202 at 0/1 and 150 uL tests whether the compact measured strong-condition result cb446680f62351d087a9 is a scaffold-wide property or a local condition effect. The current model assigns substantial width to this phosphorus-containing graph.

m202 at 10/1 and 50 uL is a loading and condition contrast to the compact measured 10/1, 150 uL record cb446680f62351d087a9. It directly tests whether the current broad prediction is a model artifact at strong solvent.

m195 at 20/1 and 100 uL bridges the intermediate-to-strong region below the measured 50/1 point 79362765eb92377a5970. It tests whether the fused aromatic aldehyde retains a broad tail or collapses like other measured high-width cases.

m141 at 2/1 and 100 uL supplies an intermediate anchor below the measured strong-condition point 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0. This is useful for learning whether the methylpyridine graph effect is gradual across solvent strength.

m141 at 20/1 and 150 uL extends the basic-aromatic response beyond the measured 10/1 point 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0. It tests strong-eluent transfer without assuming that the pyridyl ester correction applies universally.

m211 at 2/1 and 150 uL fills the low-to-intermediate condition curve below measured 10/1 and 20/1 records 810b065b0b86ff8c9aae and bd2e9fee67bbba1155df. It is a useful discriminator for the unresolved loading response of this azaaromatic scaffold.

m211 at 50/1 and 150 uL is a direct loading contrast to the measured 50/1, 50 uL and 100 uL records 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4 and 449b809e4efaaf2af86a. It tests whether the unusual loading effect persists at the strong-eluent tail.

m72 at 20/1 with DCM and 150 uL contrasts the measured DCM 20/1, 50 uL point 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 and the PE point 8e7636d7a60a6058305a. It separates loading from solvent-system effects in a strongly polar amino ester.

m72 at 0/1 with PE provides an early solvent-system anchor for comparison with the measured DCM and PE high-ratio behavior 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 and 8e7636d7a60a6058305a. The wide current interval makes this useful for limiting extrapolation of the broad tail.

m160 at 0/1 and 150 uL supplies a low-strength anchor for a donor-rich aromatic nitrile family with measured high-retention points 36d971e3231c54486d05, ad833f34f6b91872362d, and fe66b2381d33aa2ea3a8. It tests whether the strong response begins early or is threshold-like.

m216 at 2/1 and 50 uL samples the lower-strength side of the high-retention curve established by measured 5/1 and 10/1 points 33ffc69a253a89f15995 and 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321. This can improve condition transfer for the fused azaaromatic family.

m31 at 10/1 and 50 uL tests a strong predicted transition after the compact measured 1/1 point 386303f0b10c49ce93b4. It discriminates a real condition-driven increase from a broad model extrapolation for a carbonyl nitrile.

m19 at 2/1 and 150 uL is a loading contrast to the measured 2/1, 50 uL high-retention point 6d21e9ec887b3408c612. It isolates whether the amino ester response is driven by loading, condition, or graph context.

m209 at 10/1 and 50 uL fills the solvent-response curve above measured 1/1 and 2/1 points f7e3bf988bd0e1b9f58b and eda42a3c0f94ffce3e99, while remaining below the strong PE behavior 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf. It tests the onset of its late transition.

m212 at 2/1 and 50 uL provides a lower-strength anchor for a family with measured strong-condition points 942b8fc9cf013acda52b and 70cba7a21b5a01fb8e73. It can reveal whether the current high retention is already established at moderate solvent strength.

m161 at 1/1 and 150 uL bridges the measured 2/1 and 5/1 amino nitrile points e12edd0198c0d750ecd5 and a60552f4d1a5ced4641f. The label tests whether positional amino substitution creates an early onset or a late broadening branch.

m199 at 5/1 and 100 uL is a condition/loading point between the measured 1/1 result 741e52b1633ebf2743f3 and the measured 5/1, 50 uL behavior f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c. It tests whether the broad interval is condition-driven and how finish movement scales with loading.

m37 at 20/1 and 100 uL extends a carbonyl-rich aromatic response beyond the measured 10/1 point 38e6b8bf0f089fcadd80. It samples a high-width strong-eluent region that can repair condition extrapolation for related carbonyl rows.

m37 at 10/1 and 50 uL is a loading contrast to the measured 10/1, 100 uL point 38e6b8bf0f089fcadd80. It separates loading movement from the apparent strong-solvent response before selecting a universal correction.

This molecule-novel m36 point at 2/1 and 100 uL has a large current interval and probes an amino-acetophenone graph context absent from the labeled set. It tests transfer from the measured amino-ester failures d2921349ba8d9cef15a4 and c70b471334f9747d6f98 without assuming identical behavior.

The molecule-novel m36 point at 0/1 and 50 uL pairs with the 2/1 m36 experiment to form a local condition-response curve. The pair can distinguish an intrinsically delayed scaffold from a sharp response emerging near 2/1.

This molecule-novel m43 point supplies a compact aromatic-carbonyl calibration anchor at moderate solvent and has limited similarity to the measured rows. It helps prevent corrections learned from broad heteroatom-rich tails from spreading into ordinary halogenated aromatic chemistry.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-response transitions are scaffold-specific and can be abrupt between low or intermediate ratios and strong mobile phases; matched points are needed to locate their onset and curvature.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor needs condition-sensitive scaffold representations rather than a globally smooth solvent correction. Intermediate labels can teach where endpoint movement begins and whether V1 and V2 change together.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the remaining intermediate points for m90, m202, m209, m31, and related families reveal smooth transitions or scaffold-specific thresholds?

hypotheses.content: Loading changes V1 and V2 asymmetrically and the direction and magnitude are scaffold-dependent; m211 remains a particularly important counterexample to a universal loading rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model often predicts nearly invariant loading responses, while measured pairs show endpoint-specific shifts. More matched contrasts can improve both targets and prevent the model from transferring a single scaffold effect across the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected m146, m206, m90, m119, m211, m37, and m19 pairs reproduce onset-dominant movement, finish-dominant movement, or reversals?

hypotheses.content: Graph context and functional-group surroundings affect retention and solvent sensitivity beyond coarse polarity, donor, acceptor, and aromaticity counts; basic-site environment, linker topology, positional substitution, and accessibility matter.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest current failures cluster in pyridyl carbonyls, amino esters, fused alcohols, methylpyridines, and related heteroatom-rich structures. Labels from matched and molecule-novel graph contexts can improve conditional representation rather than only applying molecule-wide offsets.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural distinctions transfer across pyridyl esters, amino esters, amino ketones, fused alcohols, and other heteroatom-rich aromatic scaffolds after condition and loading are accounted for?

hypotheses.content: Broad finishes under strong or EA-rich conditions are scaffold-specific; high model width does not by itself imply a broad experimental interval.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The retrained model must distinguish genuine broad tails from artifacts caused by sparse strong-condition data. Compact labels for m202 and related strong-eluent candidates can prevent broad-tail corrections from degrading ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which high-width m202, m195, m72, m199, and related candidates retain broad finishes, and which collapse to compact intervals?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes strengthened the scaffold-specific transition hypothesis: m146 rose sharply from low ratios into the 10/1 regime, m206 showed the same delayed rise, m178 changed strongly between 10/1 and 50/1, and m28 and m90 showed steep condition responses. Loading feedback remains mixed: m146 and m11 show meaningful endpoint movement, while m211 continues to resist a universal rule. The large errors for m66, m90, m205, m86, m88, m119, and m129 support more graph-condition transfer experiments. The compact m202 outcome, together with compact m117 and m164 outcomes, further weakens blanket broad-tail extrapolation. This batch therefore moves from already well-sampled extremes toward intermediate curve points, matched loading contrasts, and molecule-novel graph anchors.
batch_rationale: The batch repairs several high-consequence regions while preserving interpretable local experiments. m146, m206, m90, m205, m119, m202, m141, m211, m72, m209, and m37 provide intermediate or loading-linked response points around measured failures and transitions. The m202, m195, m72, and m199 choices test whether broad current predictions survive measurement after compact and scaffold-specific counterexamples. m31, m19, m216, m212, and m161 extend condition-response coverage into additional carbonyl, amino, nitrile, and fused heteroatom contexts. The paired molecule-novel m36 experiments add a new amino-ketone graph environment, while m43 supplies a lower-width aromatic-carbonyl calibration point. Together these labels should improve representation of structure-condition-retention interactions, repair strong-tail failures, and limit overcorrection of common compact rows across the heterogeneous Row-distribution.
